overview.summary: Canada combines universities, colleges and polytechnics with a post-graduation work permit route. Since 2024 the government has capped study permits and tightened work-permit eligibility, so programme choice now matters a great deal.
overview.educationSystem: Universities award bachelor’s, master’s and doctoral degrees. Colleges and polytechnics offer certificates, diplomas, advanced diplomas, graduate certificates and some degrees. You must study at a Designated Learning Institution (DLI) to get a study permit.

process: Receive a letter of acceptance from a DLI.
Gather financial, academic and identity documents.
Apply online and pay the fees.
Give biometrics at a visa application centre and complete a medical exam if instructed.
Wait for a decision; then travel with your letter of introduction.

financialEvidence.requirement: Outside Quebec, a single applicant must show CAD 23,448 for living expenses for applications submitted on or after 1 September 2026, in addition to first-year tuition and travel costs. Quebec sets its own amount.

insurance.requirement: Depends on the province: some include international students in provincial plans, others require school insurance.

documents: Letter of acceptance from a DLI
Provincial or territorial attestation letter (PAL/TAL), unless exempt
Proof of financial support (for example a GIC, bank statements, education loan)
Academic documents and English test results
Biometrics and, if requested, a medical exam
NOC from Nepal’s Ministry of Education

conditions: Up to 24 hours per week off campus while classes are in session, if your permit allows off-campus work.
Unlimited hours during scheduled breaks (such as winter and summer holidays).
You must be a full-time student at a DLI in an eligible programme of at least 6 months that leads to a degree, diploma or certificate.
Working more than allowed can cost you your status and future permits. Job availability varies widely by city; do not plan to pay tuition from part-time work.

postStudyRoutes.name: Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP)

duration.value: Up to 3 years depending on programme length (master’s graduates can receive up to 3 years)
duration.label: official

postStudyRoutes.conditions: Programme of at least 8 months at an eligible DLI; language test at CLB 7 for university degrees or CLB 5 for college programmes; non-degree programmes must be in an eligible field of study for permits applied for on or after 1 November 2024.

postStudyRoutes.name: Employer-specific work permits
postStudyRoutes.conditions: Usually need a job offer and sometimes a Labour Market Impact Assessment.

postStudyRoutes.name: Permanent residence
postStudyRoutes.conditions: Express Entry and provincial programmes are competitive and points-based. A PGWP does not guarantee permanent residence.

lifestyle.text: Rental markets are tight in big cities. Arrange temporary housing first and watch for rental scams asking for deposits before viewing.
Many institutions include a transit pass in student fees. Distances between cities are large.
Long, cold winters in most provinces; budget for proper winter clothing.
Coverage depends on the province: some include international students in provincial plans, others require school insurance.
Generally safe. Learn tenant rights in your province and keep copies of your permit.
